  "codebook": {
    "definition": "Credit-claiming occurs when a Senator asserts that they are personally responsible for a desirable government action or outcome. This includes securing federal funding or grants, obtaining a favorable agency decision, delivering particularized benefits to their home state or constituents, or successfully advancing/passing specific legislation or amendments that they authored or championed.",
    "clarification": "To be classified as 'credit-claiming' (1), the text must explicitly link a realized or advanced government outcome (such as awarded funds, a passed bill or amendment, or an agency policy change) directly to the Senator's prior efforts (e.g., 'I secured', 'my amendment was included', 'I authored the legislation'). Merely expressing support for an action, introducing a bill without reporting its passage, holding a hearing, or announcing a grant without claiming any role in securing it does not count. Mentions of past successful legislative achievements do count as credit-claiming.",
    "positive_examples": [
      {
        "text": "U S Senator Charles E Schumer today announced that Westchester County has received two federal grants totaling 134 004... Schumer was among the first senators who recognized the need for the federal government to establish a funding program for local governments...",
        "explanation": "The Senator announces that particularized financial benefits (grants) have been awarded to local constituents and explicitly links the outcome to his own prior legislative efforts to establish and push for the funding."
      },
      {
        "text": "The United States Senate today passed legislation to reauthorize and expand the State Children s Health Insurance Program S CHIP... The legislation also includes an amendment co sponsored by Senator Nelson.",
        "explanation": "The Senator claims personal responsibility for a substantive policy outcome by highlighting that an amendment he championed was successfully included in the passed bill."
      },
      {
        "text": "I fully support the development and construction of this airport I helped secure an expedited environmental review from the federal government and facilitated the return of the project to the national priority list for federal funding...",
        "explanation": "The Senator explicitly states that their personal actions directly resulted in favorable government outcomes (an expedited review and a return to the priority list)."
      }
    ],
    "negative_clarification": "Texts that only demonstrate position-taking (e.g., explaining a vote or expressing an opinion), announce the mere introduction of a bill, or describe procedural steps (like hearings) without pointing to a concrete policy or funding outcome secured by the Senator should be classified as '0'. Announcing ceremonial resolutions or non-governmental local awards also does not count as credit-claiming.",
    "negative_examples": [
      {
        "text": "The U S Senate today considered two resolutions calling for a calendar timeframe and setting arbitrary dates for withdrawing American forces from Iraq Nebraska s Senator Ben Nelson voted against both resolutions because he supports setting measurable goals...",
        "explanation": "The Senator is merely explaining a vote and taking a position on a policy issue. There is no claim of having successfully secured a tangible benefit or passed a piece of authored legislation."
      },
      {
        "text": "U.S. Senators Byron Dorgan (D-ND) and Trent Lott (R-MS) will introduce legislation later today to halt the Federal Communications Commission's (FCC) 'fast march' toward easing media ownership rules.",
        "explanation": "The Senators are announcing the introduction of a bill. While they are proposing legislation, it has not yet advanced or passed, so they cannot claim credit for an actual government outcome."
      },
      {
        "text": "The Senate Finance Subcommittee on Social Security recently held a hearing on bipartisan legislation sponsored by U S Senators Susan Collins and Dianne Feinstein D CA that would protect the retirement benefits of public servants...",
        "explanation": "The text describes a procedural step (a subcommittee hearing) for a proposed bill. Because it does not announce the successful passage of the legislation or the delivery of resources, it is classified as position-taking rather than credit-claiming."
      }
    ]
  }
}
